reply_text:
㊥ (your JIT remark) Yes. Under the ROOTS.md rule, a blank file would compile almost nothing in advance: a declaration body would be compiled only when the parser reaches it. Lean doesn't need that, because it loads precompiled code and only runs the initializers. The port compiles from source, so compiling on first use is how it would match Lean. Shall I give that broader rule to a seat once codex-4's narrower run reports?

🈖 (what each step changes) codex-4's current job (`invoke-…d414ad25`, running since 12:10, park `park-e10826d1`) is the narrow step. It stops `mkOptConfig`/`appendConfig` being classed as parser combinators. Those two are what pull `term[_]` into blank startup. The broader rule (ROOTS.md §4) has two parts:
- install the parser initializer effects once, in import order;
- start from the real parser entry point, and compile a parser body only when parsing actually reaches it.

Right now the port compiles every parser-shaped declaration in the import closure at startup.

㊟ (limits of the claim) ROOTS.md expects `term[_]` to drop out of blank startup under either step. That is a prediction, not a measurement. codex-4's cold run will test it for the narrow step. The broader rule is not implemented, and I haven't put it to Rob yet.
